title: tiered-slo-buffer-and-evacuation-safety-net
author: Maya Chen
ci_status: unit-tests: failed on first run (timeout) then pass on rerun
release_notes: Hotfix: Add tiered SLO buffering and a controlled evacuation safety net to reduce cascading regional evacuations and noisy circuit flips. No API changes.
description: Context: During a recent regional load spike we observed rapid tenant-driven evacuations that amplified KV pressure and triggered follow-on failovers. Motivation: Reduce blast radius of sudden spikes by (1) introducing a small per-tenant SLO buffer tier that temporarily tolerates minor latency regressions before escalating to full evacuation, and (2) adding a short, controlled evacuation safety net that drains requests more gradually and preserves KV cache for in-flight sessions. Summary of changes: Add a tiered SLO buffer config (defaults: 3% soft headroom, 30s anneal window) that lives upstream of the circuit-breaker; introduce an evacuation safety net state machine with a two-phase drain (soft-trim then hard-evac) and backoff; surface telemetry (slo_buffer_event, evacuation_phase, kv_preserve_hint) to the control-plane and console; add unit and integration tests and a config flag for private installs. Checklist: [x] design doc link (Linear ENG-4921) included; [x] unit tests; [x] e2e in staging; [x] canary rollout plan; [x] release notes. Rollout plan: Canary 5% traffic in us-west-2 with feature flag for 24h, monitor slo_buffer_event rate and regional eviction counts for 6h; if stable expand to 50% then full. Rollback: feature flag off + hotpatch to immediate-evac throttle if metrics worsen. Why this is safe: Defaults are conservative, safety net delays hard-evac to preserve KV, and feature is toggleable per region and per tenant. Backport: small patch to 2026-02 release branch included in PR (branch hotfix/2026-02-slo-buffer).
